PROPOSED ALIGNMENT OF ACADEMIC CALENDARS Academic Calendar Committee Report #2024-2025-03 April 10, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting Rationale: When the URI Accelerated Online program began offering courses in seven-week sessions, neither the two seven-week sessions in the fall nor the two seven-week sessions in the spring were aligned with the start of URI's fall and spring semester. The resulting differences between the Academic and Accelerated Online calendars had several unexpected consequences. First, faculty who wished to teach in the Accelerated Online program could not do so as part of their AY workload. Second, some sources of financial aid linked to the Academic calendar were not available to students taking Accelerated Online courses. Third, students were prevented from taking courses in-person, full seinester online, and accelerated online courses concurrently. As a result, students are currently restricted to either classes that fall within the traditional calendar OR Accelerated Online courses. We propose changes to the University Mamual aligning the Academic and A ccc le rated Online calendars. These changes are sufficient to address concerns (1) and (2), above. While they are also necessary to address concern (3), additional legislation will be required to allow calendar to simultaneously take online accelerated courses (and vice versa).
